author: Julie Fine, Jeff Mason
description: President Donald Trump will head to Texas on Friday, promoting the economic and energy policies he’s expected to tout at his State of the Union address in the heart of one of the most hotly contested Senate primary races.
title: Trump Eyes Post-State of the Union Texas Trip Before Key Primary

author: Shawn Donnan
description: After the Supreme Court invalidated tariffs that the US had imposed using an emergency powers statute, the Trump administration swiftly invoked a different law, Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, to set a flat 10% levy on imports. President Donald Trump later said he would boost the import tax to 15%.
title: All About Section 122, Trump’s New Go-To Tariff Provision

author: Jeff Mason
description: The US is readying a spate of additional national security investigations that would enable President Donald Trump to impose new tariffs, as the administration seeks to rebuild his global tariff regime in the wake of last week’s Supreme Court ruling that struck down the country-specific emergency levies he imposed last year.
title: Trump Eyes New Trade Probes to Revive Tariffs After Court Defeat

author: Matt Shirley
description: The head of the Congressional Budget Office said the agency would recalculate its projections of US tariff revenue — recently estimated at $3 trillion over a decade — once the Trump administration finalizes its plans in the wake of Friday’s Supreme Court ruling.
title: CBO Plans New Fiscal Estimates After Trump Cements Tariff Plan

author: Zoe Tillman
description: The Trump administration is likely to face legal obstacles if it argues against refunds for the tariffs struck down by the US Supreme Court — thanks to statements by Justice Department lawyers.
title: Trump Faces Tough Legal Landscape to Oppose Tariff Refunds

description: The killing of El Mencho, the notorious CJNG cartel leader, plunged Mexico into chaos. What comes next will test President Sheinbaum, Bloomberg Opinion columnist JP Spinetto says. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: El Mencho’s Aftermath Is a Test for Sheinbaum

author: Amy Stillman, Kelsey Butler
description: Despite assurances from President Claudia Sheinbaum and her security minister Monday that Mexico was returning to normal after a weekend of cartel violence, many vacationers to Puerto Vallarta and other cities still faced canceled flights and shelter-in-place warnings.
title: Mexico Visitors Shaken After Drug Lord Death Fueled Travel Chaos

author: Lucy White
description: Reform UK plans to turn a chunk of Britain’s public sector pensions into a “sovereign wealth fund” that will “back British growth,” in a proposal likely to raise eyebrows among industry experts.
title: Reform UK Plans to Roll Pensions Into ‘Sovereign Wealth Fund’

author: Anthony Capaccio, Roxana Tiron
description: The Pentagon will accelerate development of a next-generation stealth fighter jet for the Navy after previously pushing back — a move that could benefit either Boeing Co. or Northrop Grumman Corp., which are competing to build the aircraft.
title: Pentagon Will ‘Accelerate’ Navy Fighter Despite Early Reluctance

author: Jorge Valero, Alberto Nardelli
description: A European Union assessment found that President Donald Trump’s new tariff policy will increase levies on some of the bloc’s exports, including cheese and some agricultural products, above the level permitted in their trade agreement.
title: EU Warns That Trump’s New Tariff Policy Breaks Trade Agreement

author: Greg Ryan
description: Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey banned travel for all non-essential motor vehicles in three southeastern counties that are getting battered by Monday’s winter storm.

author: Nathan R Dean
description: The administration will likely need new legal grounds to keep trade barriers in place later this year
title: Trump Has a Broad-Brush Option for His Next Move on Tariffs

author: Leah Nylen
description: The US antitrust agencies are seeking public comments to help craft new guidelines to ensure businesses can better understand when cooperation between rivals within the same industry is allowed, including when they can share data or pricing information.
title: US Regulators Plan Guide for When Business Rivals Can Share Data

author: Jimmy Jenkins
description: The state of Maryland is suing to stop the Department of Homeland Security from turning a warehouse into an immigration detention facility.
title: Maryland Sues DHS to Stop ‘Massive’ ICE Detention Facility

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Emily Graffeo discuss next legal steps after the Supreme Court struck down President Trump's tariffs with Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Policy Analyst Nathan Dean. Then, Bloomberg TV and Radio International Economics & Policy Correspondent Michael McKee joins to discuss the latest from the NABE economic conference. Plus, Bloomberg News Weather Reporter Lauren Rosenthal has the latest on the major storm that dumped snow across the Northeast and snarled travel. Also, Bloomberg News Senior Editor for Credit James Crombie has the latest on private credit worries as Blue Owl anxiety continues to rattle the sector. Finally, EY-Parthenon Chief Economist Greg Daco joins to discuss the fiscal and economic implications of changes to tariff policy. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stocks Slump on AI, Tariff Jitters | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 2/23/26

author: Kavita Mokha, Samy Adghirni
description: France said that US Ambassador Charles Kushner will no longer have direct access to French government officials after he failed to show up for a summons over State Department comments about the killing of a far-right activist in Lyon.
title: France Pulls Kushner’s Ambassadorial Access After Official Snub

author: Melos Ambaye
description: Coinbase Global Inc. has been aggressively lobbying in Washington to preserve a key revenue stream that in Bloomberg Intelligence’s estimation could multiply as much as sevenfold.
title: Coinbase Stablecoin Revenue Poised for Up to Sevenfold Surge, BI Says

description: Mexico’s government laid out details of how it located the country’s most-wanted drug kingpin, stressing that US security agents didn’t actively participate in President Claudia Sheinbaum’s most direct confrontation with the cartels yet. Maya Averbuch explains (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Mexico Details How It Took Out Its Most-Wanted Cartel Chief

(Source: Bloomberg)

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, the dollar and US futures fall after the US Supreme Court's ruling against Donald Trump's tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). The US President is now planning a 15% global tariff under Section 122 of the 1974 Trade Act. That stands to benefit countries facing higher tariffs, including China, India and Brazil. Countries which negotiated more favorable rates, including the UK, EU and Japan, risk losing out.

Today's guests: Janet Whittaker, Clifford Chance, Senior International Arbitration and Disputes Partner; Tatjana Greil Castro, Muzinich, Co-Head of Public Markets. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Winners & Losers as Trump Announces 15% Global Tariffs | Daybreak Europe 2/23/2025

description: Video recorded by AP shows the aftermath of violence after a top cartel leader was killed by Mexican authorities in the western state of Jalisco. “El Mencho" cartel leader Nemesio Rubén Oseguera Cervantes was slain in a federal operation on Sunday morning, Mexico’s government said in a statement. After the raid, criminal groups burned cars and trucks to block roads and there were also clashes between gangs and the authorities, according to local outlets Reforma and Milenio. (Source: Associated Press)
title: Killing of Mexican Cartel Boss Sparks Violence

description: US President Donald Trump said he will increase the global 10% tariff to 15%. He is applying the new baseline tariff under Section 122 of the 1974 Trade Act, which allows the president to impose tariffs for 150 days without congressional approval. Bloomberg’s Laura Davison breaks down the situation.
title: What’s Next for Trade as Trump Ups Global Tariff to 15%

description: The US and Iran are set to resume talks Thursday in Geneva, according to Omani mediators. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he expects to meet US special envoy Steve Witkoff for the talks and reiterated that Iran won’t be pressured by a US military buildup in the region. Bloomberg’s Joumanna Bercetche reports.
title: Iran-US Nuclear Talks to Resume This Week
